**No Longer Write -** _**Mochiji**_ **(** _**Record of the Ink Pool**_ **) Review from Field Visit** 

## **No Longer Write --** _**Mochiji**_ **: How does it work?** 

**==> picture [357 x 649] intentionally omitted <==**

**A digital calligraphy of the article** _**Mochiji**_ **shown on the screen. Chinese characters generated by AI through deep learning by Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). Data are collected from the works of ancient Chinese calligraphers. Viewers can send characters to the digital 'ink pool' and provide the data for the deep learning of the AI.** 

## **Past and Now: How did digitalisation change us?** 

**Past** ： **According to the story of** _**Mochiji**_ **, Wang Xizhi studied calligraphy hard near a pool. The pool turned black from the ink because Wang endlessly washed writing brushes in it. Now** ： **Calligraphy becomes less important because people write with touch screens and keyboards. The pool is replaced by a big screen.**

## **What is the role of AI in such artworks?** 

**A 'co-shaping process' (Wellner, 2022) --> AI-based artworks may be created by AI, but they are not solely made by AI. --> The involvement of humans is still necessary. In this artwork: The AI generates Chinese characters. The artists give the artwork meanings. The viewers can make a difference to the artwork, appreciate it and judge it.**
